name: Autism South Africa
summary: National non-profit providing information, guidance, training, and advocacy for autistic people and their families across South Africa's nine provinces.
notes: Registered Public Benefit Organisation; leadership structure not stated on site.

name: Autism Awareness Care and Training Centre (AACT)
summary: Accra-based centre for autistic children founded in 1998 by a nurse practitioner and parent, providing behaviour management, therapy, and individualized education plans.
notes: Parent-led, professionally run. Site returns 406 to a bare curl user agent; needs a full browser-style header.

name: Patrick Speech and Languages Centre (PSLC)
summary: Nigeria's first dedicated autism centre, opened in Lagos in 2006, offering speech and language therapy, vocational training, and a professional training academy.
notes: Parent-founded, professionally run; operates two centres in Ikeja and Lekki.

name: Autism Awareness Uganda
summary: Kampala-based community organisation of parents, professionals, and volunteers running caregiver training, awareness campaigns, and referral support for autistic people.

name: Bizchut - The Israel Human Rights Center for People with Disabilities
summary: Independent legal-advocacy and watchdog organisation advancing the rights of people with all disability types in Israel through litigation, policy work, and a public inquiries hotline.
notes: Cross-disability, not neurodiversity-specific; board combines disabled people, parents, professionals, and academics.

name: Beit Issie Shapiro
summary: Israeli nonprofit that develops, researches, and scales disability service models such as early intervention and assistive technology, and shares them internationally.
notes: Holds UN ECOSOC consultative status.

name: Shutaf Inclusion Programs
summary: Jerusalem-based "reverse inclusion" nonprofit running year-round camps and youth-leadership programs where disabled and non-disabled children and teens participate together.
notes: Direct page fetch was blocked by a bot filter; verified live via curl (200 OK) and secondary sources.

name: Lebanese Autism Society (LAS)
summary: Beirut-based membership NGO founded by parents and professionals, running educational, vocational, and consultancy programs for autistic children and teens.
notes: Runs a Technical School for Adolescents with Autism.

name: Dubai Autism Center
summary: UAE nonprofit established by government decree providing assessment, intervention, rehabilitation, and community-awareness programs for autistic children.

name: Tohum Otizm Vakfı (Tohum Autism Foundation)
summary: Istanbul-based public-benefit foundation focused on early diagnosis and special education for autistic children, and on national autism screening and awareness campaigns.

name: Action for Autism (AFA) - National Centre for Autism
summary: Delhi-based Indian non-profit, founded in 1991 as a parent support group, running assessment, education, therapy, employment, and self-advocacy services for autistic people.
notes: Runs a Self-Advocacy Programme, but it is professionally facilitated rather than self-advocate-run.

name: Bapu Trust for Research on Mind & Discourse
summary: Pune-based trust doing non-coercive, community-based mental health work, including an urban community mental health and inclusion programme; founder was active in the international Hearing Voices movement.
notes: About page 404'd during verification; leadership framing not explicitly self-declared. Site returns 406 to a bare curl user agent.

name: Ummeed Child Development Center
summary: Mumbai-based non-profit founded in 2001 by a developmental pediatrician, providing trans-disciplinary clinical services, training, and research for children with developmental disabilities.

name: Autism Society of Pakistan (ASP)
summary: National umbrella non-profit registered in 2010, running Autism Resource Centres in Rawalpindi and Islamabad offering diagnosis, therapy, school-integration support, and parent training.
notes: Board of Governors composed of professionals and affected parents. Site returns 403 to a bare curl user agent; resolves 200 with full browser headers.

name: Karachi Down Syndrome Program (KDSP)
summary: Karachi-founded nonprofit, registered in 2014, delivering family support, healthcare, education, and skills programmes for people with Down syndrome, with chapters in four other Pakistani cities.
notes: Registered as a Section 42 nonprofit company; also runs chapters in Faisalabad, Islamabad, Hyderabad, and North Nazimabad.

name: The Society for the Welfare of Autistic Children (SWAC)
summary: Dhaka-based nonprofit founded in 2000 by parents of autistic individuals, running a school, therapy services, respite care, and a social enterprise for people with autism.
notes: Executive Committee is mainly composed of parents of autistic individuals.

name: Urakawa Bethel House
summary: Social welfare corporation in Hokkaido founded in 1984 by former psychiatric patients and a social worker, practicing "Tojisha-Kenkyu" (self-directed peer research) into members' own psychiatric experiences.
notes: Explicitly by-and-for psychiatric survivors (tojisha); runs an annual 'Bethel Festival' and cooperative small businesses.

name: Japan Developmental Disabilities Network (JDDnet)
name_local: 日本発達障害ネットワーク
summary: Tokyo-based umbrella network of about 57 affiliated parent groups, academic societies, and professional bodies covering autism, ADHD, and learning disabilities nationally in Japan.
notes: Founded following Japan's 2004 Developmental Disabilities Support Law.

name: Beijing Stars and Rain Education Institute for Autism
summary: China's first NGO dedicated to autistic children, founded in Beijing in 1993 by a parent, running an autism education and training programme for children and parents.
notes: Site intermittently unreachable, verified via Wikipedia/British Council. Older autismchina.org domain is now dead.

name: Autism Society of Taiwan
summary: National civic association based in Taipei serving autistic people and families, running vocational and social training as well as diagnostic and employment support.
notes: Runs the 'Star Kids Workshop' vocational and social training programme.

name: Autism Resource Centre (Singapore)
summary: Singapore charity registered in 2000 providing lifelong services for autistic people, including Pathlight School, early intervention, employment support, and caregiver training.
notes: Runs Pathlight School, Singapore's first autism-focused school.

name: National Autism Society of Malaysia (NASOM)
summary: Malaysia's longest-running national autism body, founded in 1986, running early intervention, therapy, vocational training, and residential independent-living programmes nationwide.

name: Autism Society Philippines (ASP)
summary: National nonprofit founded in 1989 with about 16,000 members across 106 local chapters, working toward social acceptance and self-reliance for autistic Filipinos.

name: Yayasan MPATI (Masyarakat Peduli Autis Indonesia)
summary: Indonesian national foundation, evolved from a 1998 parent community, focused on training and empowering parents of autistic children and advocating for government autism support policy.
notes: Evolved from KOMPAA (Komunitas Peduli Autis dan ADHD), founded in 1998.

name: Vietnam Autism Network (VAN)
name_local: Mạng lưới Tự kỷ Việt Nam
summary: Voluntary nonprofit network of parents, autism specialists, and autistic individuals recognised by Vietnam's Ministry of Labour, running national autism awareness activities.
notes: Governing board is elected from parent-group representatives across six provinces/cities; member of the ASEAN Autism Network.

name: NeuroDiversity Association Hong Kong (NDAHK)
summary: Hong Kong advocacy organisation, established in 2024, promoting the value of neurodiversity through cross-sector partnerships, education, and conferences.

name: The Association of Parent for Thai Persons with Autism
name_local: สมาคมผู้ปกครองบุคคลออทิซึม (ไทย)
summary: Bangkok-based nonprofit working alongside the Autistic Thai Foundation on quality-of-life programmes for autistic people, including sports, digital learning, and IT skills training.
notes: Parent association; partners with the government-accredited Autistic Thai Foundation.

name: Yellow Ladybugs
summary: Autistic-led Australian organisation running community events, education, and advocacy for autistic girls, women, and gender-diverse people.
notes: CEO/founder is autistic; site states it is 'proudly autistic-led and neuro affirming'.

name: Reframing Autism
summary: Australian registered charity providing education, resources, courses, and advocacy on autism, run by and for autistic people.
notes: Operates nationally with no single fixed HQ city stated; registered with the ACNC.

name: I CAN Network
summary: Autistic-led group mentoring organisation delivering school-based and online mentoring programmes for autistic and neurodivergent young people in Australia and New Zealand.
notes: Founder is autistic; reports 77% of staff are autistic and requires a minimum of half; reaches both Australia and New Zealand.

name: Autistic Self Advocacy Network Australia and New Zealand (ASAN AUNZ)
summary: Grassroots autistic-led advocacy network doing systemic advocacy and self-advocacy skill-building across Australia and New Zealand.
notes: Binational (Australia and New Zealand); member of the Australian Autism Alliance; organisationally distinct from ASAN in the USA.

name: Rawcus
summary: Melbourne ensemble theatre company creating devised performance work with an ensemble of performers with and without disability.
notes: Originated via a partnership between Theatreworks, disability organisation Scope, and the City of Port Phillip. Site returns 406 to a bare curl user agent.

name: Altogether Autism
summary: Free, government-funded nationwide autism information and advisory service for autistic people, whanau, and professionals in New Zealand.
notes: Run in partnership between Your Way | Kia Roha and Parent to Parent New Zealand; includes an autistic-led peer offshoot, 'By Autistics for Autistics'.

name: Amaze
summary: Victoria's peak autism body, providing information, advocacy, and support for autistic people and their families.
notes: Board includes at least one autistic member alongside parents of autistic adults; not stated as autistic-led.

name: Autism New Zealand
summary: National New Zealand charity supporting autistic people and their families through a Board of Trustees and nationwide services.
notes: At least one board member is autistic and also a parent of an autistic adult; overall composition reads as ally-led/mixed.

name: Autism CRC (Cooperative Research Centre for Living with Autism)
summary: University of Queensland-based Australian research centre, established in 2013, co-funding participatory autism research and programmes such as the DXC Dandelion employment programme.
notes: Academic-run, not self-advocate-led.

name: DXC Dandelion Program
summary: Corporate autism employment initiative run by DXC Technology since 2014, in partnership with universities and Autism CRC, with 17 teams and over 250 autistic employees across Australia.
notes: Reports 92% retention rate among autistic employees; a corporate CSR programme, not autistic-led.
